nahhas-meani:1-1.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ ٱتَّقُواْ رَبَّكُمْ إِنَّ زَلْزَلَةَ ٱلسَّاعَةِ شَيْءٌ عَظِيمٌٌ﴾.
Sufyān narrated from Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqama, who said: This is before the Day of Resurrection.

nahhas-meani:10-10.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ذٰلِكَ بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ يَدَاكَ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَيْسَ بِظَلاَّمٍ لِّلعَبِيدِ﴾.
And the meaning is: it will be said to him: This punishment is because of what your hands have sent forth, and because Allah is not unjust to [His] servants.

nahhas-meani:11-11.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَعْبُدُ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ حَرْفٍ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid, who said: in doubt.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Its literal sense in the language is: on the edge of the path of religion, i.e. not having entered it wholly.
And He made this clear by His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِنْ أَصَابَهُ خَيْرٌ ٱطْمَأَنَّ بِهِ﴾.
He said: he settles down; ﴿وَإِنْ أَصَابَتْهُ فِتْنَةٌ﴾ — he said: a punishment or a calamity; ﴿ٱنْقَلَبَ عَلَىٰ وَجْهِهِ﴾ — he said: he apostatizes as a disbeliever.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿خَسِرَ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلآُخِرَةَ﴾.
And Mujāhid and Ḥumayd read: ﴿خَاسِرَ الدُّنْيَا والآخِرَةِ﴾ ("losing this world and the Hereafter", as an active participle).

nahhas-meani:12-12.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَدْعُو مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَا لاَ يَضُرُّهُ وَمَا لاَ يَنفَعُهُ﴾.
Then He said afterwards: ﴿يَدْعُو لَمَنْ ضَرُّهُ أَقْربُ مِنْ نَفْعِهِ لَبِئْسَ المَوْلَى﴾.
So it may be asked: How can it cause him harm, when He has said: "what neither harms him"?
The answer is that the meaning is: he invokes one the harm of whose worship [is nearer than its benefit].
And if it is asked: How did He say ﴿أَقْرَبُ مِنْ نَفْعِهِ﴾ when it has no benefit?
The answer is that the Arabs say of what will never be at all: This is far off — like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿ذَلِكَ رَجْعٌ بَعِيدٌ﴾.
And there are several answers concerning the verse on account of the lām:
Most grammarians hold that it is out of its place, and that the meaning is: he invokes one whose harm is indeed (la-ḍarruhu) nearer than his benefit.
And Abū al-ʿAbbās said: There is an omission in the speech, i.e. he invokes as a god one whose harm is nearer than his benefit.
And it is said: ﴿يدعو﴾ here is in the sense of "he says", as ʿAntara said:
يَدْعُوَن عَنْتَرَ وَالرِّمَاحُ كأَنَّهَا * أَشْطَانُ بِئْرٍ في لَبَانِ الأَدْهَم
(They call out "ʿAntar!" while the spears, like the ropes of a well, are in the breast of the black horse.)
And Abū Isḥāq said: It is possible that "yadʿū" is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), with an omitted hāʾ (pronoun) in it, and the khabar (predicate) of "man" is ﴿لَبِئْسَ المَوْلَى ولَبِئْسَ العَشِيرُ﴾.
Al-Farrāʾ said: It is possible that "yadʿū" is the khabar of "man", and ﴿لَبِئسَ المَوْلَى وَلَبِئْسَ العَشِيرُ﴾ is a repetition of what precedes it.
And Abū Isḥāq has another view — and he claimed that the grammarians allowed it — he said: ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ is in the sense of "alladhī" (who/which), i.e. the one who is in far error — ﴿يَدْعُوْ لَمَنْ ضَرُّه﴾ — as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿وَمَا تِلْكَ بِيَمِينكَ يَا مُوْسَى﴾?
And he recited:
عَدَسْ مَا لِعَبَّادٍ عَلَيْكِ إِمَارَةٌ * أَمِنْتِ وَهَذَا ـ تَحْمِلينَ ـ طَليقُ
(Gee up! ʿAbbād has no authority over you; you are safe, and this one you carry is set free.)
And al-Farrāʾ reported that something is possible here for which there is no precedent in transmission, namely "yadʿū li-man ḍarruhu" with a kasra on the lām, meaning he calls to one whose harm…, just as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿الحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي هَدَانَا لِهَذَا﴾, i.e. to this.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The verse is difficult because of the entry of the lām; and the skilled grammarians do not allow it to be construed as moved forward or backward, because it is not inflected (lā tuṣraf); and that ﴿يَدْعُو﴾ should be in the sense of "he says" is good, with the khabar omitted, i.e. he says: the one whose harm is nearer than his benefit is his [god].

nahhas-meani:13-13.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَبِئْسَ ٱلْمَوْلَىٰ﴾.
That is, the patron (al-waliyy), as the poet said:
فَعَدَتْ كِلاَ الفَرْجَيْنِ تَحْسَبُ أَنَّهُ * مَوْلَى المَخَافَةِ خَلْفُهَا وَأَمَامُهَا.
(She ran off, reckoning each of the two openings — behind her and before her — to be the master (mawlā) of fear.)
﴿وَلَبِئْسَ ٱلْعَشِيرُ﴾, i.e. the companion and intimate friend.
Mujāhid said: He means the idol.

nahhas-meani:15-15.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَن كَانَ يَظُنُّ أَن لَّن يَنصُرَهُ ٱللَّهُ فِي ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلآخِرَةِ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This verse is difficult, and there are two views on it:
a- Sufyān narrated from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Tamīmī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: ﴿مَن كَانَ يَظُنُّ أَن لَّن يَنصُرَهُ ٱللَّهُ﴾ — meaning Muḥammad ﷺ; ﴿فَلْيَمْدُدْ بِسَبَبٍ﴾, i.e. with a rope; ﴿إِلَى ٱلسَّمَآءِ﴾, i.e. the ceiling of his house; ﴿ثُمَّ لْيَقْطَعْ﴾, i.e. let him strangle himself.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is the view of most of the people of exegesis, among them al-Ḍaḥḥāk.
And its meaning is: whoever thinks that Allah will not give Muḥammad, upon him be peace, victory and make his religion prevail over all religion, let him exert his utmost effort, and let him see whether that will avail him anything.
b- And the other view: Ṭalḥa ibn ʿAmr said: I heard ʿAṭāʾ say concerning His saying, exalted is He, ﴿فَلْيَمْدُدْ بِسَبَبٍ إِلَى ٱلسَّمَآءِ﴾: i.e. to the ceiling (samāʾ) of his house; then let him see whether that will avail him, or bring him provision.
And Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid: ﴿مَن كَانَ يَظُنُّ أَن لَّن يَنصُرَهُ ٱللَّهُ﴾ — he said: i.e. that Allah will not provide for him.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This view too is well known in the language, and it is the view of Abū ʿUbayda.
And the people of the language report that it is said: arḍ manṣūra, i.e. rained upon.
And it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: "Whoever thinks that Allah will not help Muḥammad", i.e. provide for him in this world.
And someone else said: It is preferable that the hāʾ (pronoun) refers back to the Prophet ﷺ, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, mentioned people who worship Him on an edge, then followed that with this verse, about people who think that Allah will not grant ample provision to Muḥammad and his community, nor provide for them in the Hereafter from His sublime gifts; so let him stretch a rope to a sky above him, whether the ceiling of his house or something else, if he is enraged at the hastening of that.
Abū Jaʿfar said: We have already mentioned the discussion of His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوْا والَّذِينَ هَادُوْا﴾ in Sūrat al-Baqara.

nahhas-meani:18-18.t:
His saying, exalted is He: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَسْجُدُ لَهُ مَن فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَن فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
It is said: prostration here is obedience and submission.
And the meaning of His saying, exalted is He, ﴿وَكَثِيرٌ حَقَّ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْعَذَابُ﴾ is: and many refused.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَن يُهِنِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُ مِن مُّكْرِمٍ﴾.
Al-Farrāʾ said: It is also read «فَمَا لَهُ مِنْ مُكْرَمٍ», i.e. [no] honouring.

nahhas-meani:19-19.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هَـٰذَانِ خَصْمَانِ ٱخْتَصَمُواْ فِي رَبِّهِمْ﴾.
We have already mentioned, at the beginning of this sūra, concerning whom this account was revealed.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ قُطِّعَتْ لَهُمْ ثِيَابٌ مِّن نَّارِ﴾.
It is said: This is for one of the two disputing parties, namely the disbelieving group.

nahhas-meani:2-2.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَوْمَ تَرَوْنَهَا تَذْهَلُ كُلُّ مُرْضِعَةٍ عَمَّآ أَرْضَعَتْْ﴾.
That is, she becomes oblivious of it, abandons it and is bewildered, because of the hardship of what she is in.
And Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made clear, on the tongue of His Prophet ﷺ, at which station on the Day of Resurrection this will be. Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd al-Khāliq narrated to us: ʿUmar ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Asadī narrated to us: my father narrated to me: ʿIṣām ibn Ṭalīq narrated to us from Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind, from al-Shaʿbī, from Masrūq, from ʿĀʾisha, who said: "The Prophet ﷺ was [resting] in my lap, and my tears dropped onto his cheek, and he ﷺ woke up. I said: I remembered the Resurrection and its terror; will you remember your families, O Messenger of Allah? He said: O ʿĀʾisha, [there are] three [places] in which no one will remember anyone but himself:
a- at the Balance, until he knows whether his scale will be light or heavy;
b- at the scrolls, until he knows what is in his scroll;
c- and at the Path (al-ṣirāṭ), until he has crossed it."
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَتَرَى ٱلنَّاسَ سُكَارَىٰ وَمَا هُم بِسُكَارَىٰ﴾.
That is: you will see people drunk from the punishment and fear, yet they are not drunk from drink.
And Abū Hurayra and Abū Zurʿa ibn ʿAmr ibn Jarīr read ﴿وَتُرَى النَّاسَ﴾ ("and the people will be made to seem to you"), i.e. you will think them so because of the severity of what they are in.
Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Nāfiʿ narrated to us: Salama narrated to us: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatāda, and Abān, from Anas ibn Mālik, who said: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمْ إِنَّ زَلْزَلَةَ السَّاعَةِ شَيْءٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾ was revealed, up to His saying ﴿وَلَكِنَّ عَذَابَ اللَّهِ شَدِيدٌ﴾.
He said: It was revealed to the Prophet ﷺ while he was on one of his journeys, and he raised his voice with it until his Companions gathered back to him. He said: Do you know what day this is? This is the day on which Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, will say to Adam: O Adam, rise and send forth the party of the people of the Fire — out of every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine to the Fire and one to Paradise.
That weighed heavily on the Muslims, so the Prophet ﷺ said: "Aim for what is right, come close to it, and rejoice; for by Him in whose hand is my soul, you among mankind are only like a mole on the flank of a camel, or like the mark on the foreleg of a riding beast; and with you are two creations which have never been with anything without outnumbering it — "Gog" and "Magog" — and those who perished of the multitude of jinn and humans."

nahhas-meani:20-20.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يُصْهَرُ بِهِ مَا فِي بُطُونِهِمْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, it is melted.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The people of the language report: ṣahartu al-shaḥm, i.e. I melted the fat; and al-ṣuhāra is what is melted from the fat of the tail.

nahhas-meani:3-3.t:
Ibn Jurayj said concerning His saying, exalted is He: ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يُجَادِلُ فِي ٱللَّهِ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ﴾.
He is al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith.
And someone else said: ﴿يُجادِلُ﴾ means he disputes about Allah, by his claim that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, is not able to bring back to life one who has decayed and returned to dust — ﴿بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ﴾ (without knowledge).
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَتَّبِعُ كُلَّ شَيْطَانٍ مَّرِيدٍ﴾.
That is: and that saying and disputing of his follows every rebellious devil.
﴿كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِ﴾ — Qatāda said: "That is, upon the devil."
Al-marīd: the one who goes far in evil and oversteps in it; and from it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿قَالَ إِنَّهُ صَرْحٌ مُمَرَّدٌ مِنْ قَوَارِيرَ﴾.
It is said: elongated.
And it is said: made smooth.

nahhas-meani:4-4.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِ أَنَّهُ مَن تَوَلاَّهُ فَأَنَّهُ يُضِلُّهُُ﴾.
Mujāhid and Qatāda said: that whoever takes the devil as a patron, i.e. follows him.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And the meaning is: it has been decreed concerning the devil that he will lead astray whoever follows him.

nahhas-meani:5-5.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِن كُنتُمْ فِي رَيْبٍ مِّنَ ٱلْبَعْثِ﴾.
That is: if you are in doubt that you will be resurrected, then reflect on the beginning of your creation and your origination, for you will find no difference between beginning and repetition.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِنَّا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ مِّن تُرَابٍ﴾.
Meaning Adam ﷺ. ﴿ثُمَّ مِن نُّطْفَةٍ ثُمَّ مِنْ عَلَقَةٍ﴾.
Al-Khalīl said: al-ʿalaq is blood before it dries; the singular is «علقة»; and that is what the sperm-drop («نطفة») becomes.
Abū ʿUbayd said: al-ʿalaq of blood is that whose redness is intense.
﴿ثُمَّ مِن مُّضْغَةٍ﴾
And it is a small lump of flesh, the size of what is chewed. ﴿مُّخَلَّقَةٍ وَغَيْرِ مُخَلَّقَةٍ﴾.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda, who said: complete and incomplete.
Al-Shaʿbī said: the «نطفة», the «علقة» and the «مضغة»; when it is turned over in the fourth creation it is formed (mukhallaqa), and if [the womb] casts it out before that, it is unformed.
Abū al-ʿĀliya said: unformed means the miscarried foetus.
Abū Jaʿfar said: ﴿مُخَلَّقة﴾ means given shape; and this is made clear by this ḥadīth traced back (marfūʿ) to the Prophet ﷺ, which is narrated by various routes.
Among its routes is what Salama ibn Kuhayl narrated from Zayd ibn Wahb, who said: I heard Ibn Masʿūd say: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say — and he is the truthful, the one whose truthfulness is confirmed —: "The creation of each of you is gathered in his mother's belly for forty days; then it becomes an «علقة» for forty days; then it becomes a «مضغة» for forty days; then Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, sends an angel to it and says: Write his deeds, his term and his provision, and write him wretched or happy."
ʿAbd Allāh said: By Him in whose hand is my soul, a man works the deeds of the people of happiness — he works the deeds of the people of Paradise — until there is nothing between him and it but a forearm's length; then wretchedness overtakes him, and he works the deeds of the people of the Fire, or of wretchedness, and enters the Fire.
And ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Bakr narrated from his grandfather Anas ibn Mālik, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has appointed an angel over the womb, and he says: O Lord, a «نطفة»? O Lord, an «علقة»? O Lord, a «مضغة»? Then when Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, wills to complete its creation," he said, "the angel says: Male or female? Wretched or happy? What is the provision? And that is written in his mother's belly."
ʿAlqama said: When the «نطفة» falls into the womb, the angel says: Formed or unformed? If He says: Unformed, the womb expels it as blood. And if He says: Formed, he says: Male or female? Wretched or happy? And He says: Write it from the Preserved Tablet. So he finds its description and copies it; and the servant continues to act according to it until he dies.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِّنُبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ﴾.
That is: We have mentioned the stages of creation in order to make [things] clear to you.
And it is possible that the meaning is: We created this creation in order to make [things] clear to you.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَنُقِرُّ فِي ٱلأَرْحَامِ مَا نَشَآءُ﴾.
That is: and We settle in the wombs whatever We will.
Then He said: ﴿وَمِنكُمْ مَّن يُتَوَفَّىٰ﴾.
And Abū Ḥātim reported that someone read: ﴿وَمِنْكُمْ مَنْ يَتَوفَّى﴾ (active voice).
And its meaning is: he completes his term in full.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِكَيْلاَ يَعْلَمَ مِن بَعْدِ عِلْمٍ شَيْئاً﴾.
Al-Farrāʾ said: so that he understands nothing after having understood.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَتَرَى ٱلأَرْضَ هَامِدَةً﴾.
Saʿīd narrated from Qatāda, who said: That is, dusty and crumbled.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It is said: hamadat al-nār, when the fire is extinguished and its flame has gone; and arḍ hāmida: i.e. dry, with dust upon it.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِذَآ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْهَا ٱلْمَآءَ ٱهْتَزَّتْ وَرَبَتْ﴾.
That is: it stirs; and ﴿رَبَتْ﴾ means it increases.
And Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ and Khālid ibn Ilyās read ﴿وَرَبَأَتْ﴾, i.e. it rises until it becomes like the rabīʾa (the lookout), who is the one who keeps watch for the people from a high place; so he is rābiʾ, and rabīʾa by way of intensification.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَنبَتَتْ مِن كُلِّ زَوْجٍ بَهِيجٍ﴾.
That is: of every kind of plant.
And Saʿīd narrated from Qatāda, who said: ﴿بَهِيج﴾ means beautiful.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It is said bahuja, so it is bahij, when it becomes beautiful; and abhajanī: it delighted me by its beauty.

nahhas-meani:6-6.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ذٰلِكَ بِأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلْحَقُُّ﴾.
That is: the matter is that; the matter is what has been described and made clear to you.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَنَّهُ يُحْيِـي ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ﴾, i.e. just as He gave life to the earth by His power.

nahhas-meani:9-9.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثَانِيَ عِطْفِهِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, his neck (raqaba).
And Qatāda said: That is, his neck (ʿunuq).
Abū al-ʿAbbās said: al-ʿiṭf is the part of the neck that bends; and cloaks are called al-ʿuṭuf because they fall on that place.
And someone else said: The arrogant one who turns away in haughtiness is described by this.

nahhas-meani:25-25.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَيَصُدُّونَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
The khabar (predicate) of "inna" is omitted.
And the meaning is: Those who disbelieve have perished; as [the poet] said:
"إنَّ مَحَلاً وَإِنَّ مُرْتَحَلاً"
(Indeed there is a place of halting, and indeed there is a departure — with the khabar omitted.)
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلْحَرَامِ ٱلَّذِي جَعَلْنَاهُ لِلنَّاسِ سَوَآءً ٱلْعَاكِفُ فِيهِ وَٱلْبَادِ﴾.
And Abū Ḥātim reported that someone read ﴿سَوَاءً﴾ in the accusative, and "al-ʿākifi fīhi wa-l-bādī" in the genitive.
And the meaning is: which We made for the people — the resident and the visitor from the desert.
Mujāhid said: al-ʿākif is the one who stays, and al-bādī is the one who comes.
And al-Ḥasan and ʿAṭāʾ said: al-ʿākif is whoever is of the people of Mecca, and al-bādī is whoever is not of its people.
Mujāhid said: That is, the two are equal in revering it and in its sanctity.
And ʿAṭāʾ said: That is, no one has more right to it than anyone else.
And ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz interpreted the verse to mean that the houses of Mecca are not to be rented out.
And it is narrated from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb that he used to forbid the houses of Mecca being locked during the season of Ḥajj, and that people used to lodge wherever in them they found [a place] vacant.
And the apparent sense of the Qurʾān indicates that what is meant is "the Mosque", as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿هُمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوْا وَصَدُّوكُمْ عَنِ المَسْجِدِ الحَرَامِ﴾; because they used to bar [people] from it and claim that they were its masters; and He mentioned only the Mosque, and did not mention people's houses and dwellings.
And it is said: The two are equal in performing the rites.
And it is said: Neither of them has any precedence over the other.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَن يُرِدْ فِيهِ بِإِلْحَادٍ بِظُلْمٍ نُّذِقْهُ مِنْ عَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ﴾.
Murra narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, who said: If a man intends a sin, it is not written against him... but if he intended to kill a man in Mecca while he was in "ʿAdan Abyan", Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, would punish him. Then he recited ﴿وَمَن يُرِدْ فِيهِ بِإِلْحَادٍ بِظُلْمٍ نُّذِقْهُ مِنْ عَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ﴾.
And Hushaym narrated from al-Ḥajjāj, from ʿAṭāʾ: ﴿وَمَن يُرِدْ فِيهِ بِإِلْحَادٍ﴾ — he said: whoever worships other than Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.
And Mujāhid said: whoever does an evil deed.
And Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit said: They are those who hoard food in Mecca.
And the clearest of what has been said about it is that the meaning of ﴿بإِلْحَادٍ بِظُلْمٍ﴾ covers every act of disobedience, because the verse is general.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The root meaning of ilḥād in the language is deviation from the right course; and from it the laḥd (side-niche grave) was named — if it were straight it would be called ḍarīḥ. And from it is His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿وَذَرُوْا الَّذِينَ يُلْحِدُوْنَ في أَسْمَائِهِ﴾. It is said laḥada and alḥada with one meaning; this is the view of the people of the language, except al-Aḥmar, who reported that one says alḥada when one disputes, and laḥada when one swerves and deviates.
Saʿīd ibn Masʿada [al-Akhfash] said: The bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and the meaning is: and whoever intends in it deviation (ilḥādan) through wrongdoing.
And this, according to Abū al-ʿAbbās, is a mistake, because nothing is added without a meaning.
The view according to him is that "yurid" governs what indicates the intention.
So the meaning is: and whoever's intention is to deviate through wrongdoing; as the poet said:
أُريدُ لأَنْسَى ذكْرَهَا فَكَأَنَّما * تَمَثَّلُ لِي لَيْلَى بِكُلِّ سَبِيلِ
(I want to forget her memory, yet it is as though Laylā appears to me on every path.)
And al-Farrāʾ reported from one of the readers: ﴿وَمَنْ يَرِدْ فِيهِ بِإِلْحَادٍ﴾, from wurūd (coming).
And this is far-fetched, because one says only waradtuhu (I came to it), and one hardly says waradtu fīhi.

nahhas-meani:26-26.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذْ بَوَّأْنَا لإِبْرَاهِيمَ مَكَانَ ٱلْبَيْتِ﴾.
It may be asked: Why was the lām brought here, when He said in another place ﴿وَلَقَدْ بَوَّأْنَا بَنِي إسْرَائيلَ مُبَوَّأَ صِدْقٍ﴾?
The difference between them is that the people of exegesis said: the meaning is: We made the site of the House a mubawwaʾ for Abraham, i.e. a dwelling-place.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Its meaning is made clear to you by a ḥadīth which Abū ʿUbayd the Judge narrated to us from al-Zaʿfarānī, who said: Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr narrated to us: Sufyān narrated to us from Bishr ibn ʿĀṣim, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, who said: I heard Kaʿb al-Aḥbār say: "The House was a bit of foam upon the water forty years before Allah created the earth, and from it the earth was spread out."
Saʿīd said: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib narrated to us that Abraham — the Prophet of Allah ﷺ — came from "Armenia", and with him was the Sakīna (tranquillity), guiding him to the House, until it settled on the House as the spider settles on a home. He used to carry a stone among the stones — a stone which thirty men could, or could not, bear. He said: I said to Saʿīd: O Abū Muḥammad, Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, says ﴿وَإذْ يَرْفَعُ إبْرَاهِيمُ القَوَاعِدَ مِنَ الْبَيْتِ وَإِسْمَاعِيلُ﴾. He said: That was only after this.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَطَهِّرْ بَيْتِيَ لِلطَّآئِفِينَ وَٱلْقَآئِمِينَ﴾.
Hushaym narrated from ʿAbd al-Malik, who said: ﴿القائمون﴾ are those who pray.
Qatāda said: ﴿وَٱلرُّكَّعِ ٱلسُّجُودِ﴾: the people of prayer.

nahhas-meani:27-27.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَذِّن فِي ٱلنَّاسِ بِٱلْحَجِِّ﴾.
And al-Ḥasan read: ﴿وَآذِنْ في النَّاسِ بالحَجِّ﴾, without doubling and with a long vowel.
It is said: ādhantuhu bi-l-ṣalāt and with such-and-such, i.e. I informed him; and adhdhantu is for intensification.
And Ibn Abī Isḥāq read ﴿بِالْحِجِّ﴾ with a kasra on the ḥāʾ throughout the Qurʾān.
Mujāhid said: Abraham ﷺ said: O Lord, how shall I say it? He said: Say: "O people, answer your Lord." So it settled in the heart of every believer, and they answered with "Labbayka, Allāhumma, labbayk" — i.e. whoever performs the Ḥajj answered.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَأْتُوكَ رِجَالاً﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: That is, on foot (rajjāla).
And Mujāhid read: ﴿يَأْتُوْكَ رُجَالاً﴾.
And it is narrated from ʿIkrima: yaʾtūka rujjālan.
Abū Jaʿfar said: There are five forms said for the plural of rājil (one on foot): rājil and rujjāl, like rākib and rukkāb — and this is what is narrated from ʿIkrima; and rājil and rijāl, like qāʾim and qiyām.
And it is said: rājil and rajla, and rajl, and rajjāla; so these are five.
And what is narrated from Mujāhid is not known, and it is most likely to be without nunation, like kusālā and sukārā; if it were nunated it would be on the pattern "fuʿāl", and fuʿāl in plurals is rare.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَعَلَىٰ كُلِّ ضَامِرٍ يَأْتِينَ مِن كُلِّ فَجٍّ عَميِقٍ﴾.
And the companions of ʿAbd Allāh read ﴿يَأْتُوْنَ مِنْ كلِّ فَجٍّ عَميِقٍ﴾.
ʿAṭāʾ, Mujāhid and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: from every distant road.
Abū Jaʿfar said: al-ʿumq in the language is distance; and from it is biʾr ʿamīqa, i.e. a well whose bottom is far; and from it:
* "وقَاتِمِ الأَعْمَاقِ خَاوِي المُخْتَرَق" *
(And many a dusky land with distant reaches (aʿmāq), empty where it is crossed.)

nahhas-meani:28-28.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِّيَشْهَدُواْ مَنَافِعَ لَهُمْ﴾.
ʿĀṣim ibn Abī Razīn narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: the markets. «[Translator's note: the source reads «عاصم بن أبي رزين»; the usual chain is ʿĀṣim from Abū Razīn.]»
And Sufyān narrated from Jābir, from Abū Jaʿfar: ﴿لِّيَشْهَدُواْ مَنَافِعَ لَهُمْ﴾ — he said: forgiveness.
And ʿAṭāʾ said: whatever Allah is pleased with of the affairs of this world and the Hereafter.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The view of Jābir on this is the best, i.e. and proclaim the Ḥajj among the people so that they may come to perform the Ḥajj to which they were summoned, and it is a means to forgiveness. They do not come from every deep ravine, nor is it "proclaim among them so that they may trade" — this is very far-fetched.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَذْكُرُواْ ٱسْمَ ٱللَّهِ فِيۤ أَيَّامٍ مَّعْلُومَاتٍ﴾.
There is disagreement about "the known days", whereas we know of no disagreement about "the counted days".
Ibn Abī Laylā narrated from al-Minhāl ibn ʿAmr, from Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, who said: The known days are the Day of Sacrifice and two days after it; slaughter on whichever of them you wish, and the best of them is the first.
And this is what is known from the view of Ibn ʿUmar, and it is the view of the people of Medina.
And Hushaym narrated from Abū Bishr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said:
"The known days" are the ten [days], the Day of Sacrifice being one of them.
And "the counted days" are the days of Tashrīq, up to the end of the departure (al-nafr).
And ʿAṭāʾ, Mujāhid, Ibrāhīm and al-Ḍaḥḥāk held this view, and it is the view of the people of Kufa.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَكُلُواْ مِنْهَا وَأَطْعِمُواْ ٱلْبَآئِسَ ٱلْفَقِيرَ﴾.
ʿAṭāʾ and Mujāhid said: If you wish, eat; and if you wish, do not eat.
Abū Jaʿfar said: According to the people of the language this is [an imperative] of permission, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿وَإِذَا حَلَلْتُمْ فَاصْطَادُوا﴾.
And if it is said: Permission comes only after prohibition, so how can there be permission here when there is no prohibition in the speech?
The answer is that in the Jāhiliyya they used to forbid eating the meat of sacrificial animals, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, informed them that it is permitted to them.
Mujāhid said: ﴿البَائِسُ﴾ is the one who, when he asks you, stretches out his hand.
Abū Jaʿfar said: al-bāʾis in the language is one afflicted with buʾs, which is severe poverty.

nahhas-meani:29-29.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ لْيَقْضُواْ تَفَثَهُمْْ﴾.
Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Manṣūr al-Ḥāsib narrated to us: al-Ḥakam ibn Mūsā narrated to us: ʿĪsā ibn Yūnus narrated to us: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Abī Sulaymān narrated to us from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: al-tafath is shaving, shortening [the hair], stoning [the pillars], slaughtering, trimming the moustache and the beard, plucking the armpit hair and clipping the nails.
And so it is according to all the people of exegesis, i.e. coming out of iḥrām into the state of release; the people of the language know it only from exegesis.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلْيُوفُواْ نُذُورَهُمْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: the Ḥajj, the sacrificial offering, and everything incumbent on a person in the matter of the Ḥajj.
Abū Jaʿfar said: What Mujāhid said is well known; everything that is obligatory on a person is called a vow (nadhr).
So the meaning is: and let them fulfil what is obligatory on them in the matter of the Ḥajj.
Then He said, glory be to Him: ﴿وَلْيَطَّوَّفُواْ بِٱلْبَيْتِ ٱلْعَتِيقِ﴾.
Mujāhid and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: It is the obligatory circumambulation on the Day of Sacrifice.
And Rawḥ ibn ʿUbāda narrated from Ṣāliḥ ibn Abī al-Akhḍar, from al-Zuhrī, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "The House was named al-ʿAtīq only because Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, freed it (aʿtaqahu) from the tyrants, so no tyrant has ever prevailed over it."
And Abū Dāwūd al-Ṭayālisī narrated it from Ṣāliḥ, from al-Zuhrī, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab and Abū Salama, from Abū Hurayra, not traced back to the Prophet (ghayr marfūʿ).
And al-Ḥasan said: It was named al-ʿAtīq because of its antiquity.
And his proof is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿إِنَّ أَوَّلَ بَيْتٍ وُضِعَ للنَّاسِ لَلَّذِي بِبَكَّة﴾.

nahhas-meani:30-30.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ذٰلِكَ وَمَن يُعَظِّمْ حُرُمَاتِ ٱللَّهِ فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَّهُ عِندَ رَبِّهِِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: the Ḥajj and the ʿUmra.
And ʿAṭāʾ said: acts of disobedience.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The two views come back to one thing, except that the sacred ordinances (ḥurumāt) of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, are what He has made obligatory, commanded and forbidden, so that they must not be transgressed — as though it were that whose abandonment is forbidden.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأُحِلَّتْ لَكُمُ ٱلأَنْعَامُ إِلاَّ مَا يُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾.
It is said: game, for one in iḥrām.
And Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda, who said: carrion, and that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned.
And someone else said: It is what is recited in Sūrat al-Māʾida, from His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكُمُ المَيْتَةُ والدَّمُ ولَحْمُ الخِنْزِيرِ﴾ up to His saying ﴿وَمَا أَكَلَ السَّبُعُ إِلاَّ ما ذَكَّيْتُمْ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The view of Qatāda comprises this, because these forbidden things are kinds of carrion.
* Then He said, exalted is He: ﴿فَٱجْتَنِبُواْ ٱلرِّجْسَ مِنَ ٱلأَوْثَانِ﴾.
Al-rijs: stench.
And "min" here is for specifying the genus (li-bayān al-jins), i.e. that which is an idol.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱجْتَنِبُواْ قَوْلَ ٱلزُّورِ﴾.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has made false testimony equal to associating partners [with Him]; then he recited this verse.
And Mujāhid said: al-zūr is lying.
And it is said: associating partners (shirk).
The meanings are close; every lie is zūr, and the gravest of that is shirk.
And what the true meaning requires is: do not forbid what the idolaters used to forbid, such as their saying ﴿مَا فِي بُطُونِ هَذِهِ الأَنْعَام خَالِصَةٌ لِذُكُورِنا وَمُحَرَّمٌ عَلَى أَزْوَاجِنَا﴾, and forbidding the sāʾiba (the she-camel let loose), and similar falsehood, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿افْتِرَاءً عَلَى اللَّهِ﴾.

nahhas-meani:31-31.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿حُنَفَآءَ للَّهِ غَيْرَ مُشْرِكِينَ بِهِِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, following [the true religion].
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَن يُشْرِكْ بِٱللَّهِ فَكَأَنَّمَا خَرَّ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَتَخْطَفُهُ ٱلطَّيْرُ﴾.
That is, he is like this in his distance from the truth.
It is said: khaṭifahu yakhṭafuhu and ikhtaṭafahu yakhtaṭifuhu, when one seizes it quickly.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَوْ تَهْوِي بِهِ ٱلرِّيحُ فِي مَكَانٍ سَحِيقٍ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, far.

nahhas-meani:32-32.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ذٰلِكَ وَمَن يُعَظِّمْ شَعَائِرَ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
Mujāhid said, from Ibn ʿAbbās: It is fattening the sacrificial camels (budn), honouring them and making them fine.
And someone else said: ﴿شَعَائِرَ ٱللَّهِ﴾ is stoning the pillars and similar rites of the Ḥajj.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is not ruled out, and it is the position of Mālik ibn Anas: that the benefit at ʿArafa lasts until dawn breaks on the Day of Sacrifice; at al-Mashʿar al-Ḥarām until the sun rises; and in stoning the pillars until the end of the days of Minā. All of these are rites (shaʿāʾir), and the benefit in them is until a known time; ﴿ثُمَّ مَحِلُّهَا﴾ — all of them — ﴿إلى البَيْتِ العَتِيقِ﴾. So when the pilgrim, after these rites, circumambulates the Ancient House, he is released [from iḥrām].
And the singular of «الشعائر» is shaʿīra, because they are marked (ushʿirat), i.e. a sign is placed on them indicating that they are sacrificial offerings.
* Then He said, exalted is He: ﴿فَإِنَّهَا مِن تَقْوَى ٱلْقُلُوبِ﴾, i.e. indeed the deed [is from the piety of hearts].

nahhas-meani:33-33.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَكُمْ فِيهَا مَنَافِعُ إِلَىٰ أَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: There are two views on this other than the view of Mālik.
One of them: that "ʿUrwa" said: They are the garlanded sacrificial camels; one rides them and drinks of their milk.
And the second: Mujāhid said: They are the camels before they are garlanded; one benefits from riding them, their hair and their milk; and once they have become sacrificial offerings, he may not ride them except out of necessity.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The view of Mujāhid is, according to some, preferable, because the appointed term according to him is that they are made offerings and garlanded, whereas the appointed term is not present in the view of ʿUrwa.
And those who hold the view of ʿUrwa have adduced the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Ride it, woe to you!"
And it has been argued against him that he [the man] did not say to him: And is riding sacrificial camels forbidden?
And perhaps that was out of necessity; and this is made clear by the ḥadīth of Ibn Jurayj, from Abū al-Zubayr, from Jābir, from the Prophet ﷺ: "Ride the sacrificial animals in a fitting manner until you find a mount."

nahhas-meani:34-34.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ جَعَلْنَا مَنسَكاً﴾.
Sufyān narrated from his father, from ʿIkrima, who said: a place of slaughter.
And ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, saying: a festival.
Abū Isḥāq said: al-mansik is the place of slaughter, and al-mansak is the maṣdar (verbal noun).
* Then He said, exalted is He: ﴿وَبَشِّرِ ٱلْمُخْبِتِينََ﴾.
Sufyān narrated from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, who said: al-mukhbitūn are those who are at peace with the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.
And ʿAmr ibn Aws said: al-mukhbitūn are those who do not wrong [others], and when they are wronged they do not take revenge.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The origin of this is from al-khabt, which is low-lying, level ground.

nahhas-meani:36-36.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلْبُدْنَ جَعَلْنَاهَا لَكُمْ مِّن شَعَائِرِ ٱللَّهِِ﴾.
And Ibn Abī Isḥāq read: ﴿والبُدُنَ﴾, and the meaning is the same.
Mujāhid said: They were called budn because of their badāna.
Abū Jaʿfar said: al-badāna is fatness; it is said badana when it grows fat, and baddana when it grows old; and they were called budn because they are fattened.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَكُمْ فِيهَا خَيْرٌ﴾.
Ibrāhīm said: He rides when he needs to, and drinks of the milk.
And it is said: good in the Hereafter... And this is preferable, because if it were for this world, not making it a sacrificial camel would be better for him.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱذْكُرُواْ ٱسْمَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْهَا صَوَآفَّ﴾.
And ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd read: ﴿صَوَافِنَ﴾.
And al-Ḥasan, Zayd ibn Aslam and al-Aʿraj read: «صَوَافي».
Nāfiʿ narrated from Ibn ʿUmar: ﴿فَٱذْكُرُواْ ٱسْمَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْهَا صَوَآفَّ﴾ — he said: standing, lined up.
And Abū Ẓibyān narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿ٱسْمَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْهَا﴾ — he said: "In the name of Allah, and Allah is greatest; O Allah, from You and for You."
He said: And «صَوَافِن» means standing on three [legs].
Qatāda said: with the right foreleg hobbled.
Al-Ḥasan and Zayd ibn Aslam said: ﴿صَوَافِيَ﴾, i.e. purely for Allah, free of associating partners!
Abū Jaʿfar said: ﴿صَوَافَّ﴾ is the plural of ṣāffa; and ṣāffa, maṣfūfa and muṣṭaffa have one meaning (lined up).
And «صَوَافِنَ» is the plural of ṣāfina; one who stands is called ṣāfin, and it is used for what stands on three [legs].
And «صَوَافِيَ» is the plural of ṣāfin (ṣāfī), which is the pure, i.e. do not mention over them any name other than the name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, so that the invocation is purely for Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِذَا وَجَبَتْ جُنُوبُهَا﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, they fall to the ground.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَكُلُواْ مِنْهَا وَأَطْعِمُواْ ٱلْقَانِعَ وَٱلْمُعْتَرَّ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The best of what has been said on this — and it is what is correct in the language — is that Ibn ʿAbbās, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and al-Ḥasan said:
﴿القَانِعُ﴾ is the one who asks.
And ﴿المُعْتَرُّ﴾ is the one who presents himself but does not ask.
And Mālik ibn Anas said: The best I have heard is that «القانع» is the poor man, and that «المُعْتَرَّ» is the visitor.
And Abū Jaʿfar said: It is said qanaʿa al-rajulu yaqnaʿu qunūʿan, so he is qāniʿ, when he asks; and the people of the language recited:
لَمَالُ المَرْءِ يُصْلِحُهُ فيُغْنِي * مَفَاقِرَةُ أَعَفُّ مِنَ القُنُوْعِ
(A man's wealth, which he tends so that it relieves his needs, is more honourable than begging (qunūʿ).)
And it is narrated from Abū Rajāʾ that he read ﴿وَأَطْعِمُوا القَنِعَ﴾.
And the meaning of this differs from the first; it is said qaniʿa al-rajulu when he is content, so he is qaniʿ.
And it is narrated from al-Ḥasan that he read ﴿والمُعْتَرِي﴾; its meaning is like the meaning of al-muʿtarr. It is said: iʿtarrahu, iʿtarāhu, ʿarrahu and ʿarāhu, when one presents oneself for what he has, or seeks it.

nahhas-meani:37-37.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَن يَنَالَ ٱللَّهَ لُحُومُهَا وَلاَ دِمَآؤُهَا﴾.
It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that in the Jāhiliyya they used to sprinkle the blood of the sacrificial camels around the House, and the Muslims wanted to do that, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed this verse.
Ibrāhīm said concerning His saying ﴿وَلَـٰكِن يَنَالُهُ ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ مِنكُمْ﴾: Piety is that by which the Face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, is sought.

nahhas-meani:38-38.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُدَافِعُ عَنِ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ﴾.
He, Mighty and Majestic is He, promised them victory; then He informed them that He does not love whoever mentions a name other than His over the slaughtered animal, and said: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لاَ يُحِبُّ كُلَّ خَوَّانٍ كَفُورٍ﴾.
And ﴿خَوَّان﴾ is of the pattern faʿʿāl from khiyāna (treachery).

nahhas-meani:39-39.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أُذِنَ لِلَّذِينَ يُقَاتَلُونَ بِأَنَّهُمْ ظُلِمُواْ﴾.
There is an omission in the speech.
And the meaning is: permission has been given to those who are fought against to fight.
And al-Aʿmash narrated from Muslim al-Baṭīn, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, that he read "adhina" with a fatḥa on the hamza, and "yuqātilūna" with a kasra on the tāʾ, and said: It is the first verse revealed about fighting, when the Prophet ﷺ was driven out of Mecca.

nahhas-meani:40-40.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ أُخْرِجُواْ مِن دِيَارِهِم بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ﴾.
ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who said: It is the Prophet ﷺ and those who went out with him from Mecca.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِلاَّ أَن يَقُولُواْ رَبُّنَا ٱللَّهُ﴾.
According to "Sībawayh" this is an exception not from the first [kind] (a disjoined exception).
And someone else said: The meaning is "except for their saying: Our Lord is Allah", as a badal (substitute).
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَوْلاَ دَفْعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعْضَهُمْ بِبَعْضٍ لَّهُدِّمَتْ صَوَامِعُ وَبِيَعٌ وَصَلَوَاتٌ وَمَسَاجِدُ يُذْكَرُ فِيهَا ٱسمُ ٱللَّهِ كَثِيراً﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Mūsā narrated to us in "Qarqīsiyāʾ": Makhlad ibn Mālik narrated to us from Muḥammad ibn Salama, from Khuṣayf, who said:
As for «الصَّوَامِعُ», they are the monks' cells.
As for «البِيَعُ», they are the churches of the Christians.
As for «الصَّلَواتُ», they are the synagogues of the Jews.
As for «المساجدْ», they are the mosques of the Muslims.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning on this view is: were it not that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, repels some people by means of others, the places of prayer in which prayer is offered would have been demolished in the time of every prophet.
And it is said that ﴿يُذْكَرُ فِيهَا ٱسمُ ٱللَّهِ كَثِيراً﴾ refers back to the mosques specifically; this is the view of Qatāda.
As for His saying ﴿وَصَلَواتٌ﴾ — and prayers are not demolished — there are three views on it:
Al-Ḥasan said: "Their demolition" is their abandonment.
Al-Akhfash said: It is on the basis of an implied [verb], i.e. and prayers would have been abandoned.
And Abū Ḥātim said: It is, if Allah wills, in the sense of: places of prayer.
And it is narrated from "ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī" that he read ﴿وصُلُوبٌ﴾ with the bāʾ dotted beneath.
And it is narrated from him that he read ﴿وصُلُوْتٌ﴾ with a ḍamma on the ṣād and [on] the tāʾ dotted with two dots, and he said: They belong to the Christians.
And it is narrated from al-Ḍaḥḥāk that he read ﴿وصلُوثٌ﴾ with a dotted thāʾ, and I do not know whether he gave the ṣād a fatḥa or a ḍamma.
Except that al-Ḥasan said ﴿وصَلَواتٌ﴾ are the synagogues of the Jews, and in Hebrew it is ṣalūthā.

nahhas-meani:41-41.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ إِنْ مَّكَّنَّاهُمْ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ أَقَامُواْ ٱلصَّلاَةَ وَآتَوُاْ ٱلزَّكَـاةَ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: They are the community of Muḥammad ﷺ.
And Ibn Abī Najīḥ said: They are the rulers.
Abū Jaʿfar said: «الَّذينَ» is a badal (substitute) for «مَنْ», and the meaning is: and Allah will surely help those who, if We establish them in the land, establish prayer and give the zakāt.

nahhas-meani:45-45.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَكَأَيِّن مِّن قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْنَاهَا وَهِيَ ظَالِمَةٌ فَهِيَ خَاوِيَةٌ عَلَىٰ عُرُوشِهَا﴾.
The people of exegesis said: The meaning is "how many"; and according to the grammarians it is "ayy" to which the kāf of comparison has been prefixed, so that the implied sense became "like a great number", and the meaning is the meaning of "kam".
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَهِيَ خَاوِيَةٌ عَلَىٰ عُرُوشِهَا﴾.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda, who said: empty, with no one in it.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It is said khawat al-dāru takhwā khawāʾan, when the house is empty; and khawiya al-rajulu yakhwā khawan, when the man is hungry. And al-ʿurūsh are the roofs.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَبِئْرٍ مُّعَطَّلَةٍ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: That is, having no people.
﴿وَقَصْرٍ مَشِيدٍ﴾ — ʿIkrima said: That is, plastered.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ said: That is, with qaṣṣa, which is gypsum.
And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from al-Ḍaḥḥāk: ﴿وَقَصْرٍ مَشِيدٍ﴾ — he said: tall.
And the first view is preferable, because it is said shādahu yashīduhu when one builds it with shīd, which is gypsum, as ʿAdī ibn Zayd said:
شاَدَهُ مَرْمَرَاً وجلَّلَهُ كِلْسَاً * فَلِلطِّينِ في ذُراه وُكُوْرُ
(He built it (shādahu) of marble and coated it with lime, and the birds have nests in its heights.) «[Translator's note: the source prints «فللطين»; the verse is usually cited «فللطير» ("for the birds"), which the gloss follows.]»
But when one makes it tall and raises it high, one says of it only shayyadahu and ashādahu; and from it: so-and-so made mention of so-and-so widely known (ashāda bi-dhikrihi).

nahhas-meani:46-46.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِنَّهَا لاَ تَعْمَى ٱلأَبْصَارُ وَلَـٰكِن تَعْمَىٰ ٱلْقُلُوبُ ٱلَّتِي فِي ٱلصُّدُورِ﴾.
And in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: ﴿فَإِنَّهُ لا تَعْمَى﴾, and the meaning is the same.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The masculine is on the basis of "the matter" (al-khabar), and the feminine on the basis of "the situation" (al-qiṣṣa). «[Translator's note: i.e. the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn) and the pronoun of the situation (ḍamīr al-qiṣṣa).]»
Qatāda said: The physical sight was made a means of getting by and a benefit, while the beneficial sight is in the heart.

nahhas-meani:47-47.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَسْتَعْجِلُونَكَ بِٱلْعَذَابِ وَلَن يُخْلِفَ ٱللَّهُ وَعْدَهُ وَإِنَّ يَوْماً عِندَ رَبِّكَ كَأَلْفِ سَنَةٍ مِّمَّا تَعُدُّونََ﴾.
Isrāʾīl narrated from Simāk, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: A day of the days in which Allah created the heavens and the earth is like a thousand years of what you count.
And Shuʿba narrated from Simāk, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: A day of the days of the Hereafter is like a thousand years of what you count.
He said: And a day whose measure is fifty thousand years (the Day of Resurrection).
Abū Jaʿfar said: The second view is very good, because on it [the verse] connects with the preceding speech: they sought to hasten the punishment, so He said ﴿وَلَن يُخْلِفَ ٱللَّهُ وَعْدَهُ﴾, i.e. concerning their punishment; and a day of the days of their punishment in the Hereafter is like a thousand years of what you count in this world.
So the meaning becomes: Allah will not fail His promise concerning their punishment in this world, and their punishment in the Hereafter is more severe.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And there is another clear view about its meaning, namely that they sought to hasten the punishment, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, informed them that nothing escapes Him, and that a day with Him and a thousand years are the same, since that does not escape Him.

nahhas-meani:51-51.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ سَعَوْاْ فِيۤ آيَاتِنَا مُعَاجِزِينَ﴾.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr said: It is rather ﴿مُعَجِّزينَ﴾, i.e. holding [people] back from faith.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: ﴿مُعَاجِزِينَ﴾, i.e. opposing.
Al-Farrāʾ said: obstinately resisting.
And Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda concerning His saying, exalted is He, ﴿مُعَاجِزِينَ﴾: he said: They denied the signs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, and thought that they could frustrate Allah, but they will never frustrate Him.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a clear view.
And the meaning on it is: and those who strove against Our signs, thinking that they could frustrate Us — because they do not acknowledge resurrection, nor Paradise, nor Fire — those are the companions of Hellfire.

nahhas-meani:52-52.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ مِن رَّسُولٍ وَلاَ نَبِيٍّ إِلاَّ إِذَا تَمَنَّىٰ أَلْقَى ٱلشَّيْطَانُ فِيۤ أُمْنِيَّتِهِِ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ said: ﴿تَمنَّى﴾, i.e. he spoke.
And the people of the language said: "tamannā" means he recited; and the meaning is the same.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَيَنسَخُ ٱللَّهُ مَا يُلْقِي ٱلشَّيْطَانُ ثُمَّ يُحْكِمُ ٱللَّهُ آيَاتِهِ﴾.
Al-Layth narrated from Yūnus, from al-Zuhrī, who said: Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām informed me that the Prophet ﷺ recited in Mecca ﴿وَالنَّجْمِ إِذَا هَوَى﴾, and when he reached His saying, exalted is He, ﴿أَفَرَأَيْتُمُ اللاَّتِ وَالعُزَّى. وَمَنَاةَ الثَّالِثَةَ الأخرى﴾, he made a slip and said: "Their intercession is to be hoped for." The polytheists and those in whose hearts was a disease met him and greeted him, and he said: That was from the devil. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed ﴿وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ مِن رَّسُولٍ وَلاَ نَبِيٍّ إِلاَّ إِذَا تَمَنَّىٰ أَلْقَى ٱلشَّيْطَانُ فِيۤ أُمْنِيَّتِهِ﴾.
Qatāda said: The Prophet ﷺ was reciting and he dozed and became drowsy, and said: "Have you considered al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā, and Manāt, the third, the other? They are to be hoped for, and they are the exalted cranes (al-gharānīq al-ʿulā)." It settled in the hearts of the polytheists, and they all prostrated with him; and Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed ﴿وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ مِن رَّسُولٍ وَلاَ نَبِيٍّ إِلاَّ إِذَا تَمَنَّىٰ أَلْقَى ٱلشَّيْطَانُ فِيۤ أُمْنِيَّتِهِ﴾ to the end of the verse.

nahhas-meani:53-53.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِّيَجْعَلَ مَا يُلْقِي ٱلشَّيْطَانُ فِتْنَةً لِّلَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضٌ﴾.
﴿فِتْنَةً﴾, i.e. a test and a trial; and Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, tries with whatever He wills.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِنَّ ٱلظَّالِمِينَ لَفِي شِقَاقٍ بَعِيدٍ﴾.
Al-shiqāq is the most intense enmity.

nahhas-meani:55-55.t:
Then He, exalted is He, informed that these people do not repent and remain in doubt, and said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ يَزَالُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ فِي مِرْيَةٍ مِّنْهُُ﴾, i.e. in doubt; ﴿حَتَّىٰ تَأْتِيَهُمُ ٱلسَّاعَةُ بَغْتَةً﴾, i.e. suddenly; ﴿أَوْ يَأْتِيَهُمْ عَذَابُ يَوْمٍ عَقِيمٍ﴾.
It is said: It is the Day of Resurrection.
And the people of exegesis hold that it is the Day of Badr; Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Qatāda said that.
And Qatāda said: It reached me from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb that he said: Four verses were revealed about the Day of Badr:
﴿عَذَابُ يَوْمٍ عَقِيمٍ﴾ — the Day of Badr.
And "al-lizām" — the fighting on the Day of Badr.
And ﴿يَوْمَ نَبْطِشُ الْبَطْشَةَ الكُبْرَى﴾ — the Day of Badr.
﴿وَلَنُذِيقَنَّهمْ مِنَ العَذَابِ الأَدْنى دُونَ العَذَابِ الأَكْبرِ﴾ — the Day of Badr.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The root meaning of al-ʿuqm in the language is withholding; and from it is their saying "a barren (ʿaqīm) woman" and "a barren man", when the two are withheld from having a child.
And "a barren wind" is one that brings no cloud with rain in it.
I.e. in it is punishment.
And "a barren day" is one in which there is no good for a people.
So the Day of Resurrection and the Day of Badr — good and joy were withheld in both of them from the disbelievers.

nahhas-meani:60-60.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ذٰلِكَ وَمَنْ عَاقَبَ بِمِثْلِ مَا عُوقِبَ بِهِ﴾.
The first is not a punishment, but the first was called by the name of the second, because they are of one kind, by way of pairing (izdiwāj), just as the second is [sometimes] called by the name of the first.

nahhas-meani:63-63.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ أَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً فَتُصْبِحُ ٱلأَرْضُ مُخْضَرَّةً﴾.
Sībawayh said: I asked al-Khalīl about His saying, exalted is He, ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ أَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً فَتُصْبِحُ ٱلأَرْضُ مُخْضَرَّةً﴾, and he said: This is an affirmative statement (wājib), and it is a call to attention.
And the meaning is: Take note — Allah has sent down water from the sky, and it was thus and thus. «[Translator's note: i.e. the question is not a real question, so «فَتُصْبِحُ» is not put in the subjunctive as its answer.]»
And al-Farrāʾ said: It is a statement (khabar).
And it is also read ﴿فَتُصْبِحُ الأَرْضُ مَخَْضَرةً﴾, i.e. having greenery, as one says mabqala and masbaʿa, i.e. having herbs, and having wild beasts.

nahhas-meani:65-65.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيُمْسِكُ ٱلسَّمَآءَ أَن تَقَعَ عَلَى ٱلأَرْضِ إِلاَّ بِإِذْنِهِِ﴾.
And the meaning is: out of aversion to its falling.

nahhas-meani:67-67.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ فَلاَ يُنَازِعُنَّكَ فِي ٱلأَمْرِ﴾.
That is: so let them not dispute with you; and this is indicated by ﴿وَإِنْ جَادَلُوكَ﴾.
And it may be asked: They did dispute with him, so how did He say ﴿فَلاَ يُنَازعُنَّكَ﴾?
The answer is that the meaning is: so do not dispute with them.
And this is permissible only in what can only take place between two parties, such as disputing, contending and the like; if you said "lā yaḍribunnaka" (let him not strike you) meaning "do not strike them", it would not be permissible.
And it is also read ﴿فَلاَ يَنْزِعُنَّكَ فِي الأَمْرِ﴾ — "Abū Mijlaz" read it so — i.e. so let them not overcome you.
And the people of the language report: nāzaʿanī fa-nazaʿtuhu (he contended with me and I overcame him).

nahhas-meani:72-72.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَكَادُونَ يَسْطُونَ بِٱلَّذِينَ يَتْلُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ آيَٰتِنَا﴾.
Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb said: That is, they [almost] fall upon them.
And al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: That is, they [almost] seize them with the hand.
And the people of the language report: saṭā bihi yasṭū, when one assaults him, whether by striking or by insulting.

nahhas-meani:73-73.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ ضُرِبَ مَثَلٌ فَٱسْتَمِعُواْ لَهُ﴾.
Al-Akhfash said: If it is asked: Where then is the likeness (mathal)?
The answer is that there is no likeness there; the meaning is that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: They have set up a likeness for Me, according to their claim.
And al-Qutabī said: O people, your likeness is the likeness of one who worships gods that are unable to create a fly, and from whom the fly has snatched something, and they are unable to rescue it from it.
So he held that there is something in the speech indicating the likeness, namely His saying ﴿لَن يَخْلُقُواْ ذُبَاباً وَلَوِ ٱجْتَمَعُواْ لَهُ﴾ to the end of the verse.
And the position of al-Akhfash is that the disbelievers set up a likeness to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, i.e. made for Allah a like by worshipping other than Him as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, is worshipped; as He said: "Where are My partners?"
And dhubāb (fly), according to the people of the language, is singular; its plural is adhibba and dhibbān.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ضَعُفَ ٱلطَّالِبُ وَٱلْمَطْلُوبُ﴾.
The seeker is the gods, and the sought is the fly.

nahhas-meani:74-74.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَا قَدَرُواْ ٱللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ﴾.
That is, they did not magnify Him as His greatness deserves.
And having told of the weakness of what they worship, He told of His own strength, and said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَقَوِيٌّ عَزِيزٌ﴾.

nahhas-meani:77-77.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ ٱرْكَعُواْ وَٱسْجُدُواْ﴾.
So there is no bowing except with prostration.
* Then He said, exalted is He: ﴿وَاعْبُدُواْ رَبَّكُمْ﴾, i.e. make your worship purely for Allah alone.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱفْعَلُواْ ٱلْخَيْرَ﴾.
That is, everything that Allah has commanded.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ﴾, i.e. so that you may be in hope of success.

nahhas-meani:78-78.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَجَاهِدُوا فِي ٱللَّهِ حَقَّ جِهَادِهِ﴾.
It is said: This is abrogated, and it is like His saying ﴿اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ تُقَاتِهِ﴾, which was abrogated by ﴿فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُمْ﴾.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هُوَ ٱجْتَبَاكُمْ﴾, i.e. He has chosen you; then He said ﴿وَمَا جَعَلَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِي ٱلدِّينِ مِنْ حَرَجٍ﴾.
Abū Hurayra said: The burden (iṣr) that was upon the Children of Israel has been removed from you.
Yūnus narrated from al-Zuhrī, who said: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān asked ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās about His saying, exalted is He, ﴿وَمَا جَعَلَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِي ٱلدِّينِ مِنْ حَرَجٍ﴾, and he said: It is constriction; He has made a way out through the expiations for oaths. I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say that.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The root meaning of ḥaraj in the language is the most severe constriction. And it has been said that the meaning is that He granted the traveller [permission] to break the fast and to shorten the prayer, and for one unable to pray standing [permission] to pray sitting, and if he is unable [to do that], to make gestures; so He, Mighty and Majestic is He, did not constrict.
And Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda, who said: "This community has been given three things which were given only to a prophet:
a- It used to be said to a prophet: Go, there is no blame (ḥaraj) on you; and it was said to this community: ﴿وَمَا جَعَلَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِي ٱلدِّينِ مِنْ حَرَجٍ﴾.
b- And the Prophet ﷺ is a witness over his community; and it was said to this community: ﴿وَتَكُونُواْ شُهَدَآءَ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ﴾.
c- And it used to be said to a prophet: Ask and you will be given; and it was said to this community: ﴿وَقَالَ رَبَّكُمُ ادْعُوني أسْتَجِبْ لَكُمْ﴾."
And Kaʿb al-Aḥbār said something similar to this.
And ʿIkrima said: He made lawful [marrying] women two, three and four.
And it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: He made repentance acceptable.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مِّلَّةَ أَبِيكُمْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ﴾.
That is, it has been made wide for you as it was made wide for him ﷺ; and it is said: ﴿وَافْعَلُوْا الخَيْرَ﴾ — the doing of your father Abraham.
* Then He said, exalted is He: ﴿هُوَ سَمَّاكُمُ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ مِن قَبْلُ وَفِي هَـٰذَا﴾.
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās; he said, saying: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, named you.
Mujāhid said: ﴿مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾, i.e. in the Books and the Reminder.
Abū Jaʿfar said: ﴿وَفِي هَذَا﴾ means the Qurʾān.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِيَكُونَ ٱلرَّسُولُ شَهِيداً عَلَيْكُمْ﴾.
Sufyān said: That is, concerning your deeds; ﴿وَتَكُونُواْ شُهَدَآءَ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ﴾ — that the messengers conveyed [the message] to them.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَنِعْمَ ٱلْمَوْلَىٰ﴾, i.e. the patron; ﴿وَنِعْمَ ٱلنَّصِيرُ﴾, i.e. the helper — as one says qadīr and qādir, raḥīm and rāḥim.
